skill.name: airunway-aks-setup
skill.description: Guide AI Runway setup on an existing AKS cluster, from cluster checks to first model deployment.
skill.summary: Set up AI Runway on AKS from verification to a working model deployment.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many Markdown command examples, relative links, and PowerShell notes, but most are false positives rather than hidden executable code. The remaining risk is operational: the skill guides privileged AKS changes, token secret creation, and endpoint validation. No evidence of prompt injection, obfuscated payloads, or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Privileged Kubernetes operations can affect production clusters.
remediation.suggestion: Show the active context and namespace before changes, require explicit confirmation, and recommend least-privilege Kubernetes access.

remediation.issue: Gated model setup handles HuggingFace tokens and Kubernetes secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Use short-lived tokens when possible, avoid logging secrets, restrict secret RBAC, and delete secrets after testing.

remediation.issue: Model endpoint smoke tests and ingress guidance may expose services.
remediation.suggestion: Validate endpoint ownership, use harmless test prompts, and require authentication and network policy before external ingress.

semantic_findings.title: Privileged Kubernetes Administration Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill guides kubectl and make operations that can install providers, deploy model resources, inspect workloads, and change AKS state. The actions match the skill purpose, but they need explicit user approval and verified cluster context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited instructions are explicit Kubernetes administration workflows that can alter cluster resources. The skill also requires confirmation before installation, so the risk is operational rather than malicious.

semantic_findings.title: HuggingFace Token Secret Handling
semantic_findings.description: The skill asks for a HuggingFace token, writes it to a temporary local file, and creates a Kubernetes secret for gated models. The workflow includes cleanup controls, but the token still requires secret management and access controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The token prompt, temporary file, and Kubernetes secret creation are directly documented. The local mitigations are clear, but credential exposure remains a real consideration.

semantic_findings.title: Model Endpoint Exposure Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The smoke-test flow retrieves a deployment endpoint and suggests later ingress configuration for external access. This is expected validation, but users should verify endpoint ownership and add authentication before sending real data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The endpoint retrieval and smoke test are explicit and limited to deployment validation. The external access recommendation is legitimate but can increase exposure if deployed without controls.

content.user_title: Set Up AI Runway on AKS
content.value_statement: Teams need a repeatable path from an AKS cluster to a working AI Runway deployment. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through verification, provider setup, model deployment, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Checks AKS context, node inventory, and GPU availability before setup.
Guides AI Runway controller and CRD installation from the repository root.
Maps GPU types to dtype, attention backend, and model sizing guidance.
Recommends KAITO, Dynamo, or KubeRay based on hardware and serving needs.
Creates ModelDeployment guidance for gated and non-gated starter models.
Provides Bash and PowerShell variants for setup and validation commands.
limitations: Requires an existing AKS cluster and access to kubectl, make, and curl.
Does not provision AKS clusters or GPU node pools by itself.
Commands can change cluster state and create cloud compute costs.
Model choices depend on current provider support and available GPU capacity.

use_cases.title: Onboard a Platform Cluster
use_cases.description: Verify an existing AKS cluster, install AI Runway components, and confirm provider readiness.

use_cases.title: Launch a Starter Model
use_cases.description: Select a model that fits available GPU memory and deploy it through a ModelDeployment resource.

use_cases.title: Validate Serving Readiness
use_cases.description: Check GPU constraints, endpoint readiness, and rollback steps before broader rollout.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the airunway-aks-setup skill to verify my current AKS context, node inventory, and GPU availability. Do not install anything yet.

prompt_templates.title: Install AI Runway Controller
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the airunway-aks-setup skill from step 2. Check whether the controller is already installed, then ask before running install commands.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Provider and Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the airunway-aks-setup skill to assess my GPU profile, recommend an inference provider, and suggest a starter model that fits my cluster.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy and Validate Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the airunway-aks-setup skill from step 5 to deploy a confirmed model, monitor readiness, run a smoke test, and summarize rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Verify my cluster before AI Runway setup.
output_examples.output: A readiness report with current context, node count, GPU types, missing tools, and whether setup can continue.

output_examples.input: Recommend a model for one L4 GPU.
output_examples.output: A model recommendation with memory fit, provider choice, dtype notes, and token requirements.
A deployment summary with controller status, provider readiness, model status, endpoint validation, and next operational steps.

best_practices: Run verification first and confirm the target cluster context before installation.
Ask for explicit approval before controller, provider, model, or rollback actions.
Use least-privilege Kubernetes access and rotate tokens used for gated models.
anti_patterns: Do not run setup against an unknown or production cluster without confirming context.
Do not paste HuggingFace tokens into shell history or shared logs.
Do not deploy large GPU models before checking VRAM, dtype support, and cost impact.

faq.question: Does this skill create an AKS cluster?
faq.answer: No. It assumes an AKS cluster already exists and focuses on AI Runway setup and model deployment.

faq.question: Can it work without GPUs?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents a CPU-only path using KAITO with llama.cpp and a small quantized model.

faq.question: Does it support Windows users?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes PowerShell variants for key Bash-specific setup and validation steps.

faq.question: Why does it need confirmation before commands?
faq.answer: Several steps can install controllers, deploy providers, create secrets, or apply model resources in Kubernetes.

faq.question: What tools must be installed locally?
faq.answer: The skill expects kubectl, make, and curl, plus access to the AI Runway repository root.

faq.question: How are gated models handled?
faq.answer: The skill prompts for a HuggingFace token and creates a Kubernetes secret for models that require access approval.
